issues.failure_explanation: The asserted pointwise Leibniz rule is false. On the torus take $\alpha = 1$ (so $(-\Delta)^{\alpha/2}=(-\Delta)^{1/2}$) and $f=\sin x_1$, $g=\sin 2x_1$, which lie in $H^\alpha$ for every $\alpha$. Then $fg=\tfrac12(\cos x_1-\cos 3x_1)$ and $(-\Delta)^{1/2}(fg)=\tfrac12(\cos x_1-3\cos 3x_1)$, while $f(-\Delta)^{1/2}g+g(-\Delta)^{1/2}f=3\sin x_1\sin 2x_1$. At $x_1=2\pi/3$ the left side equals $-7/4$ and the right side equals $-9/4$ with the paper's constant $C(1)=\max\{1,2^0\}=1$, and $-7/4\le-9/4$ fails; the pair $(\sin x_1,\cos x_1)$ instead forces $C=1$ exactly, so no universal constant exists. Moreover, under the stated hypotheses ($f,g\in H^\alpha$, $\alpha\le1$ in 2D) the right-hand side is not even defined pointwise, since $(-\Delta)^{\alpha/2}g\in L^2$ only and $H^\alpha\not\subset L^\infty$; the constant $\max\{1,2^{\alpha-1}\}$ is the integer-power inequality constant $(a+b)^\alpha\le2^{\alpha-1}(a^\alpha+b^\alpha)$ and does not extend to fractional powers. No proof is given (a bare citation), and the estimate is applied in conv_lemma at exponent $(1+\alpha)/2\ge1$, outside $(0,1)$ where any such rule is known to hold.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw the pointwise rule and substitute the correct $L^2$ fractional Leibniz estimates (Kato-Ponce-Vega type), which are valid for exponents in $(0,1)$; for the exponent $(1+\alpha)/2\ge1$ needed in conv_lemma no such rule exists, so the application must be re-derived (see ISSUE-002).
issues.overall_effect: The product estimate is the tool used to control the nonlinear term in the $H^{1+\alpha}$ energy estimate of conv_lemma; as a false statement it invalidates that step (independently of the further error in est_nonl, see ISSUE-002), and with it the uniform bounds bd1-bd3, the convergence claim of conv_lemma, the well-posedness theorem thm:exisuq, its continuation remark remk_extnsn, and the use of bd3 in thm:spectral_accuracy.
issues.title: False pointwise Leibniz rule for the fractional Laplacian (product estimate lemma)
issues.why_classification: The lemma is an auxiliary tool whose correct replacement (the standard Kato-Ponce-Vega inequality) is a contained, citation-level repair preserving its intended role; the collapse of the downstream a priori estimate is caused by the independent invalid inference in est_nonl (ISSUE-002), not by this lemma's repair.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and Sobolev embedding $H^{1+\alpha}(\Omega) \hookrightarrow L^\infty(\Omega)$:

issues.failure_explanation: The differential inequality $\frac{d}{dt}\|u_N\|_{1+\alpha}^2 \le C\|u_N\|_{1+\alpha}^3$ with $C$ independent of $N$ — the basis of bounds bd1-bd3, the Arzela-Ascoli compactness, and the whole convergence argument — is not established. In est_nonl the first product-rule term satisfies $\left|\left(u_N(-\Delta)^{\frac{1+\alpha}{2}}\partial_{x_1}u_N, (-\Delta)^{\frac{1+\alpha}{2}}u_N\right)\\right| \le \|u_N\|_\infty\|u_N\|_{2+\alpha}\|u_N\|_{1+\alpha}$ by Cauchy-Schwarz, but the proof bounds it by $\tfrac12 C(\alpha)\|\partial_{x_1}u_N\|_\infty\|(-\Delta)^{\frac{1+\alpha}{2}}u_N\|^2$, silently replacing $\|u_N\|_{2+\alpha}$ by $\|u_N\|_{1+\alpha}$ (false in general, e.g. $u_N=\cos(Nx_1)$); the correct estimate via the Kato-Ponce inequality loses one derivative, $\frac{d}{dt}\|u_N\|_{1+\alpha}^2 \le C\|u_N\|_\infty\|u_N\|_{1+\alpha}\|u_N\|_{2+\alpha}$, which cannot close with $N$-independent constants, and the only $L^\infty$ bound in the cited Lemma lem:inverse_inequalities is $\|\partial_{x_1}u_N\|_\infty \le 3N\|u_N\|_{1+\alpha}$, which would make the existence time $\bar T$ shrink with $N$. In addition, the embedding $\|\partial_{x_1}u_N\|_\infty \le C\|u_N\|_{1+\alpha}$ used here and in the uniqueness argument requires $H^{1+\alpha}(\mathbb{T}^2) \hookrightarrow W^{1,\infty}$, i.e. $\alpha>1$; it fails at the endpoint $\alpha=1$ (the stated embedding $H^{1+\alpha}\hookrightarrow L^\infty$ does not control the gradient). Hence bd1-bd3, the uniform convergence, and the 'strong solution' conclusion of conv_lemma are all unsupported, and the endpoint $\alpha=1$ of the claimed range $[1,2]$ is not covered.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No source-supported repair exists: both devices used (the pointwise product rule and the $H^{1+\alpha}\hookrightarrow W^{1,\infty}$ embedding at $\alpha=1$) are invalid, and the correct energy estimate provably loses a derivative, so the uniform $H^{1+\alpha}$ bound requires a genuinely new a priori argument (e.g. $X_{s,b}$-type or conservation-law-based estimates); whether such an $N$-independent bound holds on a fixed time interval is not addressed by the source.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's central convergence lemma ('the crucial result of this paper') has no valid proof: the uniform $H^{1+\alpha}$ bound (bd3) is the foundation for the existence/uniqueness theorem thm:exisuq, the continuation in remk_extnsn, and the spectral accuracy theorem thm:spectral_accuracy (which invokes bd3), so all of these become unreliable.
issues.title: Invalid $H^{1+\alpha}$ energy estimate in the convergence lemma: dropped $H^{2+\alpha}$ factor (derivative loss) and uncovered endpoint $\alpha=1$
issues.why_classification: Every supported resolution needs essentially new proof architecture, and the central lemma together with the two main theorems (well-posedness thm:exisuq and spectral accuracy thm:spectral_accuracy) has no surviving proof as written; the advertised regime $\alpha\in[1,2]$ is not established even at the level of the a priori bound.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The proofs of Theorem \ref{thm:proj_error} and Lemma \ref{lem:time_error} follow the approach developed by Deng \cite[Theorem 2.1]{deng2017optimal} for the Kawahara equation.

For brevity and to maintain focus on the novel aspects of our spectral discretization for the fZK equation \eqref{eqn:fZK}, we omit the detailed proofs and refer readers to \cite[Theorem 2.1]{deng2017optimal} for the complete methodology.

issues.failure_explanation: The algebraic projection estimate (eq:proj_erro) and the time-derivative version (lem:time_error), on which the entire optimal-rate analysis rests, are proved nowhere: the only justification is an analogy with Deng's theorem for the one-dimensional fifth-order Kawahara equation, while the adaptation (fractional Laplacian of order $\alpha$, second dimension, time-dependent advection coefficient $u$) involves nontrivial new coercivity and duality steps that are not even sketched. The exponential-convergence sketch additionally contains a reversed Stirling inequality ($r! \le r^r e^{-r}$, false since Stirling gives $r! \sim \sqrt{2\pi r}\,(r/e)^r \ge r^r e^{-r}$) and asserts the analytic growth bound $|w|_r \le r!\|w\|$ without proof or a stated radius hypothesis.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Carry out the duality-based error analysis for the modified projection in the 2D fractional setting (coercivity of $\mathcal L = K + u\partial_{x_1} - (-\Delta)^{\alpha/2}\partial_{x_1}$ plus the duality argument) and redo the exponential derivation with the correct Stirling asymptotic and an explicit analytic-growth hypothesis on $|w|_r$; contained but nontrivial.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised optimal rates $\|u(t)-u_N(t)\\le CN^{-r}$ and $Ce^{-\sigma N}$ in thm:spectral_accuracy are derived exclusively from these two unproven estimates, so the headline convergence theorem is unsupported.
issues.title: Key projection error estimates (algebraic and exponential) stated with no proof; exponential sketch uses a reversed Stirling inequality
issues.why_classification: A contained, nontrivial argument (the referenced duality technique, properly adapted) most likely restores the stated rates, so the result and its advertised scope survive; the repair is a new proof of the two estimates, not a new global proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: ((u-\widetilde{\Pi}_N u) \partial_{x_1}(\widetilde{\Pi}_N u), \mathcal E_N)& \leq (\|\partial_{x_1}(u-\widetilde{\Pi}_N u)\\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)} + \|\partial_{x_1}u\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)})\|u-\widetilde{\Pi}_N u\|\|\mathcal E_N\|

issues.failure_explanation: The estimate of the term $((u-\widetilde{\Pi}_N u)\partial_{x_1}\widetilde{\Pi}_N u, \mathcal E_N)$ uses $\|\partial_{x_1}w\|_{L^\infty} \le C|w|_2$, i.e. the embedding $H^2(\mathbb{T}^2) \hookrightarrow W^{1,\infty}(\mathbb{T}^2)$, which is false in two dimensions ($s > k+n/2$ fails: $2 \not> 1+1$); only $H^{2+\epsilon} \hookrightarrow W^{1,\infty}$ holds. Moreover, with $\|u-\widetilde{\Pi}_N u\| \le N^{-r}|u|_r$ the first product is $N^{2-2r}|u|_r^2\|\mathcal E_N\|$, not $N^{-2r}$ as written: the algebra drops a factor $N^2$. Given the (false) embedding the rate would still follow for $r\ge2$ after correcting the bookkeeping, but the valid $H^{2+\epsilon}$ replacement yields a contribution $N^{2+\epsilon-2r}$, which preserves the rate $N^{-r}$ only for $r > 2+\epsilon$; the endpoint $\alpha=1$ (i.e. $r=2$, where eq:proj_erro only allows $l \le \min\{r,\alpha+1\}=2$) is not covered. As written, the estimates do not yield $\|\mathcal E_N\| \le CN^{-r}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Re-estimate the term using $\|\partial_{x_1}(u-\widetilde{\Pi}_N u)\\|_\infty \le C\|u-\widetilde{\Pi}_N u\|_{2+\epsilon} \le CN^{2+\epsilon-r}|u|_r$ (valid for $r>2+\epsilon$) and correct the Young-inequality bookkeeping ($N^{2+\epsilon-2r}$ instead of $N^{-2r}$); this recovers $CN^{-r}$ for $\alpha>1$ and excludes or separately treats $\alpha=1$.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the headline estimate $\|u(t)-u_N(t)\ \le CN^{-r}$ (eq:L2_error_bound) is invalid as written; the result may survive for $\alpha>1$ after re-estimating the term, but the endpoint $\alpha=1$ in the theorem's scope is not established, and the fully discrete error claim at the end of Section 5 inherits the failure.
issues.title: False Sobolev embedding in 2D and rate algebra error in the spectral accuracy proof
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained re-estimation of one term (interpolate $H^{2+\epsilon}$ and fix the algebra) that preserves the advertised rate for $\alpha>1$; the loss is limited to the endpoint $\alpha=1$, leaving a recognizably comparable result.

issues.failure_explanation: Substituting $u = U(\xi)$, $\xi = (x-ct)\cos\theta + y\sin\theta$, into the ZK equation (zkeqn) gives $-cU + \cos\theta\,U'' + \tfrac12 U^2 = 0$, whose solitary wave is $U = 3c\,\mathrm{sech}^2\!\big(\tfrac{\sqrt c}{2\sqrt{\cos\theta}}\,\xi\big)$: the width parameter must be $\frac{\sqrt c}{2\sqrt{\cos\theta}}$, not $\frac{\sqrt c}{2}$. The displayed formula is off by the factor $1/\sqrt{\cos\theta}$ in the argument of $\mathrm{sech}^2$; e.g. at $c=1$, $\theta=\pi/3$ the displayed $U = 3\,\mathrm{sech}^2(\xi/2)$ gives $-cU + \cos\theta\,U'' + \tfrac12U^2 = -\tfrac{U}{2} + \tfrac{U^2}{4} \neq 0$. It is a solution only for $\theta = 0$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the missing factor $1/\sqrt{\cos\theta}$ in the argument of $\mathrm{sech}^2$ (one-line correction); all experiments and results stand since they use $\theta=0$.
issues.overall_effect: No formal result is affected — both numerical examples use $\theta=0$, where the formula is correct — but the formula is wrong for any simulation at a nonzero angle $\theta$.
issues.title: Displayed solitary wave is not a solution of the ZK equation for $\theta \neq 0$
issues.why_classification: A short, local, forced correction preserves every substantive claim, guarantee, and numerical result; nothing mathematical is lost.
